checkpoint_review: The Router's verdicts are largely accurate. It correctly identified the geometric and material features of the puck (shape, ridges, matte finish) as present. Crucially, it marked 'Printed league logos...' as false because the text is gibberish, which is a rigorous interpretation of 'functional markings'. The untestable checkpoints (sound, weight) were correctly excluded. I agree with all assessments; the Router was not too lenient.
artifact_review: The Router identified 'text_gibberish' (Severity 4.0) and 'texture_anomaly' at label edges (Severity 2.0). The Image Text Auditor confirmed the text is nonsensical ('GTA' with low confidence), supporting the high severity of the text artifact. The Topology Auditor showed a clean mask, suggesting the boundary bleeding is subtle (consistent with Severity 2.0). The Perceptual Auditor found no global distortions. I agree with the severities; the text failure is the dominant defect.
alignment_reasoning: The object is structurally a perfect hockey puck (confirmed by Fine Grained Classifier with high logit score 7.48). However, the failure to render coherent branding/text means it fails the 'Functional Components' checkpoint for markings. It aligns well with the physical class but fails the semantic/detail expectation of a manufactured product.
artifact_reasoning: Severe text hallucination on the label (gibberish characters) is a major artifact (Severity 4). Minor edge bleeding between the label and rubber body (Severity 2) further degrades realism. These artifacts prevent the image from achieving high fidelity despite correct geometry.
